messages:
jess: heads up — v2.1-int4 canary showed up in A/B. eval-bot flagged a negative delta on the 'legal' doc-summarize slice. canary is still at 5% traffic. any quick take?

eval-bot: automated alert: slice=legal metric=exact_match ab_delta=-2.7% threshold=-1.5% p=0.002 sample=1,200. action_recommendation=hold and notify.

liam: seeing the alert. can you paste the eval config + quant bits so we can triage?

jess: sure, quick config:```
model: v2.1-int4
baseline: v2.1-fp16
slices: [legal, longform, user-help]
metric: exact_match
rollout_policy: canary(5%) -> promote if ab_delta >= -1.5%
quant: nf4-int4 symmetric, per-channel
```

sam: what's the slice breakdown? legal might be skewed (long docs, citations). any shift in context length distribution?

maria: we ran a short kv-precision check. for ctx_len>2048 tokens int4 popped hallucination-ish responses on multi-ref summaries. small example: `> generated claim: 'court affirmed'` when source said 'remanded'.

liam: CI on the reported delta? could be sampling noise. if CI excludes zero we should honor the gate.
jess: CI is [-3.4%, -2.0%] — not noise. looks systemic for that slice.

sam: ok. rollout policy says auto-fallback when delta < -1.5% for primary metric. do we want immediate rollback for canary?

jess: I vote rollback. also run targeted stress: long-context KV precision, masked-token stability, and int8-hybrid quick pass.

maria: +1. I'll queue a targeted shadow run with 2k seeded legal docs focusing on citations and >2k tokens.

liam: ops-bot — please flip canary back to baseline and create a rollback job. keep the audit log.

ops-bot: actioned: rollback started for canary (v2.1-int4) -> baseline (v2.1-fp16). rollback_job=33721. canary_traffic=0%. audit_link=https://console.internal/rollbacks/33721

jess: thanks. once shadow runs finish we can decide next: re-quantize (per-channel vs per-tensor), adjust kv cache numeric path, or restrict int4 to short-context routes. ping @nina when you have findings.

liam: will follow up with a short post-mortem and a suggested change to the canary gate: require slice-aware pass + tightened CI for first 24h on high-risk slices.

sam: noted. moving this to watchlist. :eyes:

jess: closing loop here — thx all.
